sections.content: How many people stayed in Tamworth after gaining qualifications?

Tamworth is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Tamworth does not have its own university.

Tamworth has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Tamworth ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,760 state-school pupils from Tamworth who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 900 (24%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,280 (34%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Tamworth to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Tamworth's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Tamworth in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Tamworth move to?

Of Tamworth's graduates, 330 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 70 of those graduates (21%) were living fairly locally, in the Birmingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Tamworth's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 300 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 115 of those qualified non-graduates (38%) were living fairly locally, in the Birmingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Tamworth's GCSE cohort:

  • 215 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands
  • 110 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 22% of graduates and 19% of qualified non-graduates living in Tamworth had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 720 graduates and 1,185 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Tamworth. This is compared with the 900 graduates and 1,280 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of the graduates had also lived in Tamworth as GCSE pupils, while 22% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Tamworth in 2018 to 2019, 81% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 19% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
